policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: "Except ye be circumcised" renders either the aorist passive subjunctive or the present; ASV does not mark the aspectual difference.
"after the custom of Moses" is the same English with or without the article before the dative; nothing in ASV distinguishes it.

ASV opens the verse "And when Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension"; the inferential ouv would give "therefore"/"so", which ASV does use where it renders that particle (e.g. "They therefore" in v. 3).
ASV "passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria" renders the te ... kai correlative; without te the English would read simply "Phoenicia and Samaria".
Both spellings of the city name are rendered "Jerusalem" in ASV; the English cannot distinguish them.
"they were received of the church" fits either compound of dechomai; ASV draws no distinction.
"received of the church and the apostles" renders the agent phrase the same under either preposition.
ASV "And the apostles and the elders were gathered together" is the ordinary rendering of either connective particle here.
"much questioning" renders the simplex or the compound noun alike; the marginal notes on this verse concern "from early days" and "good tidings", not this word.
ASV reads "God made choice among you" — second person, matching en hymin; the alternative has en hemin, which would give "among us".
"giving them the Holy Spirit" follows "bare them witness", so the object pronoun is carried by English idiom whether or not autois stands in the Greek.
An orthographic variant of the same negative; "he made no distinction" renders either form.
"a people for his name" renders the bare dative as readily as the dative with epi; ASV does not show which stood in its text.
"the ruins thereof" translates the perfect participle of either verb of demolition; the Amos citation note settles nothing here.
"the Lord" carries the English definite article regardless of whether the Greek article is present.
ASV "who maketh these things known" has no "all"; the RP reading tauta panta would require "all these things".
ASV ends the verse at "known from of old" and has nothing answering to "known unto God are all his works"; the long RP addition is absent from the English.
"that they abstain from the pollutions of idols" renders apechesthai with the bare genitive or with apo identically.
The presence or absence of the Greek article leaves "from what is strangled, and from blood" unchanged.
An article whose presence is not reflected in the English of v. 22; ASV does not distinguish it.
"Judas called Barsabbas" suits either the simplex or the compound participle; ASV renders both verbs "call" and no note marks a difference.
"and they wrote thus by them" supplies "thus" to introduce the quoted letter, which English idiom requires whether or not tade stands in the Greek.
ASV reads "The apostles and the elders, brethren", with no conjunction before "brethren"; the RP reading kai hoi adelphoi would require "and the brethren".
ASV text reads "certain who went out from us", rendering the participle; the mapped textual_variant note "Some ancient authorities omit who went out" places the omission in the margin, not the text.
ASV has nothing answering to "saying, Ye must be circumcised and keep the law"; it moves straight from "subverting your souls" to "to whom we gave no commandment".
A case variation in the participle agreeing with "us"; "it seemed good unto us... to choose out men" is unaffected.
Word order only: both readings yield "to the Holy Spirit".
Word order only: both readings yield "these necessary things".
ASV has the plural "things strangled" here, against its singular "what is strangled" in v. 20; the plural answers pnikton, the RP singular pniktou would give the v. 20 wording.
ASV "came down to Antioch" renders the compound katelthon; the simplex elthon would be simply "came".
ASV "unto those that had sent them forth" renders the participle with its object, not "unto the apostles"; and ASV prints no verse 34 about Silas remaining.
Word order only: "Paul said unto Barnabas" either way.
ASV reads "visit the brethren" with no possessive; the RP addition hemon would give "our brethren".
Word order only: both readings yield "every city".
"was minded to take" renders either the imperfect of boulomai or the aorist of bouleuomai; ASV does not distinguish them.
ASV "to take with them John also" renders the adjunctive kai, which the RP reading omits.
Present against aorist infinitive of the same verb; "to take with them" is unchanged.
ASV "And there arose a sharp contention" renders de; the inferential oun would be rendered "therefore" or "so", as ASV does elsewhere in this chapter.
ASV reads "to the grace of the Lord", not "of God".
The Greek article before Cilicia is not reflected in "through Syria and Cilicia"; ASV does not distinguish it.
